elements.text: A consistent page layout makes long reports easier to read. Use a clear hierarchy of headings and group related text and graphics together.

The purpose of this report

Describe the question, the evidence and the proposed action. Keep the type size and line spacing consistent across the publication.

Organizing information

Use upper and lower case. Set body copy in Times Roman at 10 to 12 point. Use italic for emphasis and reserve bold for occasional distinctions.

Place related paragraphs together. Use the surrounding margins to give the page room instead of separating every small element.

Charts and illustrations

Include a graphic when it communicates relevant information. Keep line weights and rendering styles consistent.

Colour and contrast

Use black text on a light ground. Limit coloured type to a few larger headings where it improves understanding.

Source and interpretation

State the source, unit and period next to each table or graphic. Give the reader enough context to interpret the evidence.

pages.title: Four signatures.
pages.name: Main elements
pages.subtitle: Each a symbol and a unique configuration of the corporate typeface, Times Roman. Only one signature is used at a time.

elements.text: CORPORATE: THE COMPANY AS A WHOLE
Symbol and logotype are inseparable: neither is used alone, and their relative positions and proportions never change. Signatures always come from the official reproduction proofs.

pages.title: Corporate colours.
pages.name: Corporate colours
pages.subtitle: Green and blue in the symbols only, black for the logotypes. A single-colour signature where colour is not warranted.

rows: PMS 314; coated: 25% yellow, 90% cyan, 20% magenta; uncoated: 15% magenta
the flame and the H both in corporate blue; never two blues

pages.title: Backgrounds and value.
pages.name: Backgrounds
pages.subtitle: Positive forms on backgrounds of 0 to 20% value, reverse forms on 80 to 100%. Values between are avoided. Colour signatures on white only.

pages.title: Incorrect usage.
pages.name: Incorrect usage
pages.subtitle: Incorrect use gives the impression of disunity. Each of these is a rule.

rows: The symbol sits immediately left of its logotype, never above it.
The symbol is never decoration, pattern or border, and never used alone.
Green over blue in the H; all black unless all three colours are used.
Only corporate blue; otherwise all black. Never two blues.
All of the logotype is black; it is never reset or highlighted.
Never abbreviated, never rearranged onto one line.
A coloured single-colour signature on white only; colour signatures without background control go black.
No white forced inside the symbol: inside and outside are one background.
A reverse signature is all white.

pages.title: Times Roman.
pages.name: Corporate typeface
pages.subtitle: Used throughout all communications done in type, upper and lower case in regular weight. All-capitals settings are incorrect.

elements.text: 10 to 12 point for text, lines of 35 to 55 characters. The company name is set without spaces: B.C.Hydro. Black on white, or on no more than 20% value; reverse type avoided. This reconstruction sets Times Roman in TeX Gyre Termes.

relatedMarks.use: The locomotive identifies “the BCE route”. It is separate from the four official signatures and must not be placed close to the Rail signature (printed p. 2). documents.label: Report cover, text page and back cover

motion.note: The 1983 Graphic Standards Manual predates screen motion and says nothing about it. These studies are brandkit’s example of how the identity could move under the manual’s rules; they are not BC Hydro guidance.

rules.title: The signature arrives whole.
rules.text: Symbol and logotype are inseparable in the manual, so every logo study ends on the complete signature, its positions and proportions unchanged.

rules.title: Colour stays in the symbol.
rules.text: Green and blue move only inside the ring; the logotype stays black. No other colours, no glows, no gradients.

rules.title: Loops are for waiting.
rules.text: Only the symbol loops, never the full signature, and only while something loads.

rules.title: Still is a valid frame.
rules.text: With reduced motion, every study shows its final frame. Nothing depends on the animation to be understood.

studies.name: Ring
studies.timing: draw + slow, 40 ms stagger · move, settle
studies.description: The ring draws round, the two stars set inside it, then B.C.Hydro rises letter by letter.

studies.name: Current
studies.description: Blue rises and green falls into the ring and meet; then the logotype is uncovered left to right.

studies.name: Typeset
studies.description: The symbol is there from the first frame; the logotype sets one letter at a time, as on a 1983 phototypesetter.

studies.name: Alternating
studies.use: Page and app loading, 32 px and up
studies.description: The two stars take turns, green and blue, like alternating current. Symbol only; stops when loading ends.

studies.name: Charge
studies.description: A quarter of the ring runs round it while the stars hold still. At rest the ring is whole.

studies.name: Meter
studies.description: A bar fills in three steps, corporate green on the light tint, with blue marks at each step.

studies.name: End card
studies.description: Corporate blue sweeps across the frame, then the symbol sets in white in the middle.

patternCollection.description: New supporting studies informed by the 1983 system’s circular construction, green and blue, and the movement of water and energy. These abstract graphics are contemporary kit explorations, not patterns prescribed by the historical manual. Keep the official signature complete and separate from the patterned field.

manualAudit.title: BC Hydro 1983: manual coverage and overlay review
manualAudit.summary: All 48 source pages are inventoried against the kit. The audit includes original/reconstructed page overlays, template mappings, the report-cover rules and both BCE route vectors. Coverage does not mean an exact facsimile or an authenticated production master.
limitations: The four signature masters remain PofBC reconstructions; Times Roman is represented by TeX Gyre Termes and screen colours approximate the specified inks.
The illustrated cover still needs its original high-quality illustration. The tinted panel is marked as a placeholder.
Undimensioned form trims, spine thicknesses and example canvases are identified as reconstruction choices. Three-dimensional signs still require the official large-scale drawings.

H18: Both BCE route variants are now present on Rail stationery and available separately in Logos.
H21: The legal-size tender layout is now present; scan break marks are excluded from the printable form.
H22: The employee-transfer layout is present; its snap-set trim is scan-derived.
H23: The compact service layout is present; its trim and compact header placement are scan-derived.
H25: Cover rules can be shown or hidden. Both standard back-cover sizes now omit the signature and use a 6 point printing code.
H26: The ⅓-width, ¼-depth, 36/36 and 18/18 rules are implemented and follow editable cover text. Scan overlay is available.
H27: Text/grid are implemented; the illustration area remains a disclosed placeholder, with the original visible in the overlay.
H29: Broad and narrow spine examples are now present, with source rules and example dimensions distinguished.
H31: A text-page template applies the written typography principles; it is a new example, not a source facsimile.
H34: Display, single-column and classified advertisement variants are represented.
H36: Portable-panel half-cap clearance is implemented. Three-dimensional fabrication remains dependent on official large-scale drawings.
H37: Written out-of-home and specialty-media guidance is covered in the audit; this page supplies no fixed production template.
